mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in the federal funds rate over two consecutive months signals a tightening cycle that raises discount rates and reduces present value of future corporate cash flows, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS rises by >0.25% month-over-month for two consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of triggered episodes, or the rank information coefficient over triggered windows is not statistically significant at the 5% level.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in real personal consumption expenditures (proxied by GDPC1) over two consecutive quarters indicates weakening aggregate demand, which reduces corporate earnings expectations and drives negative S&P 500 returns over the subsequent 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 falls for two consecutive quarters
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 60% of triggered episodes, or the mechanism fails when unemployment is simultaneously falling.

mechanism_narrative: A rapid increase in the unemployment rate above 6.5% within a single month signals deteriorating labor market conditions, which depresses consumer spending and corporate margins, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE crosses above 6.5% in one month
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are positive in more than 40% of triggered months, or the effect reverses when inflation is simultaneously rising above 4%.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained contraction in industrial production (INDPRO) below its 12-month moving average for three consecutive months indicates supply-side weakness, which raises input costs and lowers profit margins, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO < 12-month moving average for 3 consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are not significantly different from zero during triggered periods, or the effect is absent when energy prices are simultaneously falling.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous rise in both the federal funds rate and core CPI above their respective 12-month averages signals a dual monetary-inflationary pressure, which increases discount rates and erodes real earnings, producing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS and CPIAUCSL both exceed 12-month moving average in the same month
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day returns are positive in more than 50% of triggered months, or the mechanism fails when GDP growth is accelerating.

mechanism_narrative: A coordinated surge in both personal consumption expenditures (GDPC1) and housing starts (HOUST) above their 12-month moving averages in the same month signals a robust demand recovery, which boosts earnings expectations and drives positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 and HOUST both exceed 12-month moving average in the same month
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are not significantly positive in more than 60% of triggered months, or the effect is absent when labor market indicators are weak.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in payroll employment (PAYEMS) above its 12-month moving average for four consecutive months signals strengthening labor demand, which supports consumer spending and corporate profitability, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS exceeds 12-month moving average for four consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day returns are not significantly positive in more than 50% of triggered periods, or the effect reverses during periods of rapidly rising inflation.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent decline in real retail sales (RSAFS) below its 12-month moving average for six consecutive months signals a broad-based weakening in consumer demand, which reduces corporate revenue and profit expectations, producing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: RSAFS < 12-month moving average for six consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day returns are not significantly negative in more than 70% of triggered periods, or the effect is absent when credit spreads are simultaneously narrowing.
